contains:
a { width & : .5px } a { width : .5px } a { width & : .5px } a { width : .5…
      -> \61 { \77 idth & : .5px } \61 { \77 idth : .5px } \61 { \77 idth & : .5px }…
why: a declaration, selector or block that is invalid or left open, which the printer writes back as authored, escape included
`width&:` is no declaration and `.a+.5m` no selector, so the number in either is written back as authored
a statement opening no `{}` block is a parse error the spec drops, whether the input ends in it or a block's `;` or `}` ends it (§5.4.3); css-tree keeps it as raw text
